thought.text: The `mv` moved the directory. Let me re-extract cleanly:

reasoning_content:
Strange — `ls` showed `/tmp/fvm/fvm` existing. Maybe `mv` succeeded and moved `/tmp/fvm` to `/usr/local/bin/fvm`, but then `chmod +x /usr/local/bin/fvm` — no wait, that should work even for a directory. Hmm, `chmod +x` on a directory works fine (the execute bit on directories is needed in the first place to enter them). So the chain is: `mv fvm /usr/local/bin/` moves the directory. `chmod +x /usr/local/bin/fvm` on the directory → OK. `fvm --version` → not found → the whole thing reported as an error.

But then in the next command, after `rm -rf /usr/local/bin/fvm`, `cp /tmp/fvm/fvm` fails — because /tmp/fvm was moved. And /usr/local/bin/fvm was deleted. So now fvm is completely gone. Let me re-extract from the tarball in /tmp (fvm.tar.gz should still exist).

action.command: cd /tmp && rm -rf fvm fvm.tar.gz && curl -sL --max-time 120 -o fvm.tar.gz https://github.com/btwld/fvm/releases/download/4.3.2/fvm-4.3.2-linux-x64.tar.gz && tar xzf fvm.tar.gz && install -m 0755 /tmp/fvm/fvm /usr/local/bin/fvm && fvm --version
